lyrics:
[Intro: plucked nylon guitar loop, soft xylophone, shaker]

[Verse 1: male, quiet, almost reasonable]
We still like the same six photos
We still know the same nine friends
You wave to me at weddings
Like the edge of something ends
I said we'd keep it civil
And I meant it, and I do
I only want to know the rules
For rooms with me and you

[Chorus: male voice leaps an octave, full band]
So who gets the Hendersons?
Who gets Sam and Jo?
Who gets New Year's at the lake house?
And who's supposed to know?
I could stand to lose a lover
I could learn to sleep alone
But you took the mutual friends

[Verse 2: female, cool, the loop and bass only]
Funny how you want them now
You never knew their kids
I sent the cards, I made the calls
I showed up when you hid
You stayed home with your records
While I drove to every do
They were never mutual, love
They put up with you

[Chorus: both voices, his high, hers answering]
So who gets the Hendersons?
(They were mine)
Who gets Sam and Jo?
(They were mine)
Who gets New Year's at the lake house?
And who's supposed to know?
I could stand to lose a lover
I could learn to sleep alone
But you took the mutual friends

[Bridge: band drops to xylophone and voices]
Mutual
(Were they?)
Mutual
(Were they?)

[Final Chorus: both voices at full strength, strings]
I could stand to lose a lover
I could learn to sleep alone
But you took the mutual friends
(I only took my own)

[Outro: plucked loop alone, slowing]
The mutual friends
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 129 BPM, 4/4, D minor. Small, precise and tense, then suddenly loud.

VOICE: A man with a soft, slightly reedy tenor who sings the verse quietly and evenly, then jumps a full octave into a strained, wounded shout for the chorus. A woman with a cool, clear, slightly smoky voice who delivers her verse calmly and with an edge, then answers him in the chorus.

INSTRUMENTS: A two-bar loop of plucked nylon-string guitar. A simple xylophone melody that sounds like a nursery tune. Shaker and soft hand percussion. A deep, plain bass. A sparse kick and snare in the choruses. A wavering flute-like synth. Strings in the final chorus.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the guitar loop and xylophone. 0:15 Verse 1, the man, quiet. 0:59 Chorus 1, he leaps up and the band enters. 1:29 Verse 2, the woman, over loop and bass. 2:13 Chorus 2, both voices. 2:50 Bridge, xylophone and two words traded. 3:05 Final chorus, short, both at full strength. 3:27 Outro, the loop alone, slowing to a stop at 3:45.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-2010s art-pop: dry, close and hand-made, with very few elements and a lot of dynamic range.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The octave leap on the first line of the chorus at 0:59.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The fight is over who keeps the friends, the lake house weekends and the pews at weddings. That is how separations go in middle age, and her verse lands harder because it is so practical.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Politeness, grievance, a calm correction, doubt.
